segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the rollout details and make sure the quote lines up before I send it back through deal desk.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. We’re still at 48 seats for phase one, right? That’s 35 standard users and 13 manager seats.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. I have 48 total seats, annual term starting September 1st, with implementation kicking off the week of August 12th. The subscription is $54,720 for the year, and services are $6,500 one-time.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. On the services, can that be invoiced separately? Our finance team wants the subscription on the software budget and implementation on the operations budget.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, we can split that into two invoices. I’ll note that in the billing tool: subscription billed on contract signature, services billed at kickoff. Does that work?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yes. And payment terms were net 30? I saw net 15 on the first draft.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Good catch. Your approved terms are net 30. I’ll update the order form before sending the final version.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. For go-live, we’re targeting October 7th. Is that still realistic if kickoff is August 13th?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, that should be fine. It gives us about eight weeks. The only dependency is getting your user list and two sample workflows by August 20th.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s manageable. Send the final order form to me and copy procurement, and I’ll route it for signature.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it today by 3:00 p.m. Eastern, with the net 30 terms, split invoicing, and the October 7th go-live noted in the CRM.
